title: Adjuvant ribociclib + endocrine therapy

agents.name: Ribociclib
agents.explanation: Ribociclib blocks CDK4 and CDK6, proteins that help cells move through the cycle of division. Endocrine therapy reduces the hormone signal that can drive HR-positive breast cancer.
agents.watch: Keep blood and ECG appointments. Fever, jaundice, fainting, palpitations, severe rash or new breathlessness need prompt advice.
risks: Rare serious lung or skin reactions

agents.name: Non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor ± ovarian suppression
agents.alias: Letrozole or anastrozole; ovarian suppression when indicated
agents.explanation: An aromatase inhibitor lowers oestrogen production. Premenopausal patients need an agreed ovarian-suppression plan; men also require the appropriate hormonal partner plan. The endocrine schedule continues separately from the ribociclib breaks.
agents.watch: The endocrine medicine continues during the ribociclib week off. Report troublesome joint, menopausal or injection-site symptoms.
risks: Hot flushes, joint pain and fatigue
Bone loss with AI / ovarian suppression

context_label: Adjuvant · HR-positive / HER2-negative early breast cancer
purpose: For eligible higher-risk HR-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer, ribociclib is added to endocrine therapy to reduce recurrence risk.
schedule_summary: Ribociclib 400 mg once daily on Days 1–21, followed by Days 22–28 off, for up to 3 years. The aromatase inhibitor continues daily on its own schedule; ovarian suppression is added when indicated.

phases_title: Each phase in your treatment plan
phases_note: The order depends on the indication and your recovery. The whole-treatment map shows how local treatment and ongoing medicines relate to each other.
medicines_title: Your medicines and their different roles
timeline_note: Planned treatment days are distinct from broad possible symptom patterns. Symptoms can occur outside these bands.
safety_note: There are no guaranteed safe days. Fever, shivers, sudden illness, new breathing problems or severe symptoms need prompt advice on any day, including a treatment break.
teachback: Which medicines are you taking now? What changes in the next phase? Which checks are due and who reviews them before treatment?
consent_support: Discuss the active phase, supportive medicines, fertility / menopause, treatment alternatives, monitoring, urgent contacts and when the plan will be reviewed.
urgent_extra: Report new breathlessness, jaundice, marked bleeding, severe diarrhoea, inability to drink, chest symptoms or a severe rash promptly.

support.title: Support for this phase
support.text: Agree symptom medicines with the oncology pharmacist because many anti-sickness and other medicines can affect QT or CYP3A interactions. Do not automatically reuse a chemotherapy antiemetic prescription.

support.title: Bloods and cardiac checks
support.text: Review prior toxicity → FBC, renal, liver and electrolytes → FBC / renal / liver every 2 weeks. Repeat ECG around Cycle 1 Day 14.

support.title: Visits and practical support
support.text: Ask about travel, work, fertility, menopause, exercise and help at home. The team arranges and reviews clinical checks; the patient should not have to calculate the monitoring timetable.

support.title: Follow-up and bone health
support.text: If an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression is prescribed, assess fracture risk and baseline DEXA as indicated. Repeat timing depends on the result, risk and bone treatment; it is not an automatic scan for everyone.

questions.q: What changes in the next phase?
questions.a: Ribociclib 400 mg once daily on Days 1–21, followed by Days 22–28 off, for up to 3 years. The aromatase inhibitor continues daily on its own schedule; ovarian suppression is added when indicated.
Your team should confirm the next test, who books it, and who reviews the result before treatment. The map shows expected intervals; it does not track completed tests.

questions.q: Does every scan follow a fixed schedule?
questions.a: Annual mammography; no routine markers / CT if well. New symptoms can require earlier assessment.

Usually completed in the prior adjuvant pathway → Agree sequencing before starting ribociclib → Concurrent ribociclib / RT is not assumed → Any new RT needs oncology coordination → Endocrine may continue during RT as agreed

questions.q: Which checks are baseline, and which happen during treatment?
questions.a: Days 1–21: ribociclib. Days 22–28: break. The endocrine partner follows its own schedule. Day 25–26 is a local operational option, not an NCCP replacement for early checks.

evidence.title: NATALEE · 4-year exploratory analysis (2025)
evidence.intro: Read the study population and endpoint alongside the numbers.
evidence.population: Randomised phase III study of ribociclib plus a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor versus the aromatase inhibitor alone in eligible stage II–III disease.
evidence.interpretation: Four-year invasive disease-free survival was 88.5% versus 83.6%, an absolute difference of 4.9 percentage points. Overall-survival data were immature in this analysis. This is a dated analysis, not a claim that it is the latest follow-up.

chapters.title: Before starting and between visits
chapters.intro: Plan the tests, access and support before the first dose.

items.title: Blood tests
items.text: Review prior toxicity → FBC, renal, liver and electrolytes → FBC / renal / liver every 2 weeks → Before each of the next 4 cycles; electrolytes at start of first 6 → Then as clinically indicated; written local review schedule

items.title: Heart checks
items.text: Review QT-risk medicines → ECG: QTcF must be <450 ms to start → Repeat ECG around Cycle 1 Day 14 → Additional ECG if indicated → Repeat for symptoms, QT change or interacting drugs

chapters.title: Imaging, local treatment and follow-up
chapters.intro: The whole pathway has several connected parts.

items.title: Scans and imaging
items.text: Confirm early-breast stage → No routine metastatic CT schedule → Assess symptoms promptly → Mammography according to follow-up plan → Annual mammography; no routine markers / CT if well

items.title: Radiotherapy relationship
items.text: Usually completed in the prior adjuvant pathway → Agree sequencing before starting ribociclib → Concurrent ribociclib / RT is not assumed → Any new RT needs oncology coordination → Endocrine may continue during RT as agreed

items.title: Bone health
items.text: If an aromatase inhibitor or ovarian suppression is prescribed, assess fracture risk and baseline DEXA as indicated. Repeat timing depends on the result, risk and bone treatment; it is not an automatic scan for everyone.

phases.label: Ribociclib + endocrine therapy
phases.detail: Each 28-day cycle has 21 days taking ribociclib and 7 days off. A clinical review confirms each restart.

phases.label: Endocrine therapy continues
phases.detail: Stopping ribociclib does not automatically stop the endocrine medicine or ovarian suppression. Bone-health and symptom review continue.

day_groups.title: Your reference cycle
day_groups.body: Ribociclib 400 mg once daily on Days 1–21, followed by Days 22–28 off, for up to 3 years. The aromatase inhibitor continues daily on its own schedule; ovarian suppression is added when indicated.
day_groups.action: Check the agreed prescription and contact the team for new symptoms. Restart only after the team confirms the plan.

chronology_notes.title: Treatment bands
chronology_notes.text: Show the planned medicine schedule, subject to review and dose changes.

chronology_notes.title: Symptoms
chronology_notes.text: Can occur at any time; broad bands are not measured risk curves.

chronology_notes.title: Checks and restart
chronology_notes.text: Keep the arranged blood / heart appointments. A calendar day alone does not authorise the next dose.

chronology_notes.title: Day 25–26
chronology_notes.text: An optional local pre-cycle review window, not a universal NCCP requirement. Early two-weekly tests and the Cycle 1 Day 14 ECG remain necessary.

logistics.title: Your practical treatment plan
logistics.intro: Ribociclib 400 mg once daily on Days 1–21, followed by Days 22–28 off, for up to 3 years. The aromatase inhibitor continues daily on its own schedule; ovarian suppression is added when indicated.

steps.title: Before dispensing
steps.text: Confirm blood tests, interactions, the exact tablet strengths and the plan for missed doses.

steps.title: Taking tablets
steps.text: Ribociclib 400 mg once daily on Days 1–21, followed by Days 22–28 off, for up to 3 years. The aromatase inhibitor continues daily on its own schedule; ovarian suppression is added when indicated.

steps.title: Review before restarting
steps.text: The team confirms blood results, side effects and the next prescription. Never double a missed dose or restart held treatment without advice.

details.title: Missed or vomited dose
details.text: Do not take an extra dose. Follow the medicine-specific instructions and ask the team if uncertain.

details.title: Safe handling
details.text: Swallow tablets whole, keep them in their original packaging away from children, and return unused tablets to pharmacy.

details.title: Practical arrangements
details.text: Confirm who supplies the tablets, who arranges tests, who reviews results and your urgent contact route.

anatomy: Baseline ECG and an ECG around Cycle 1 Day 14. Fainting or palpitations need urgent advice.
Keep liver blood tests. Yellow skin / eyes, dark urine or marked upper-abdominal discomfort: call promptly.
Blood counts guide whether the next cycle can start. Fever, shivers or sudden illness: contact oncology immediately.
New cough or breathlessness needs prompt assessment, even between visits.
